subject: Acme Health — SIEM & trace export options for private deployment
content:
-----Original Message-----
From: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@acmehealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sen <priya.sen@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Security Team <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 21 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIEM/export requirements for our private deploy

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Our security team captured a short list of what they need from Redwood to onboard logs/traces from our private deployment (VPC + on-prem bridge). I've attached the spreadsheet with fields they requested — retention windows, PII tagging, signing, and an initial throughput estimate.

High level asks:
- Support syslog over TLS (RFC 5425) and Splunk HEC over HTTPS with token auth
- Option for a forwarder inside their subnet (Fluent Bit) vs agentless push from Redwood egress
- Trace sampling metadata (span_id, trace_id, service.name) exported to their trace collector endpoint
- Evidence that export traffic can be pinned to a single egress IP and use mTLS

Can your engineering team confirm feasible patterns and any blockers (ports, protocols, cert requirements)? Also please share a short runbook we can give to their infra team.

Cheers,
Marco
Security Architect
Acme Health

Attachment: acme_siem_requirements.xlsx

-----Reply from Lauren Bishop to Acme Health-----
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Priya Sen <priya.sen@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Security Team <security@acmehealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIEM/export requirements for our private deploy

Hi Marco — great to have this captured. Attaching a concise runbook (lauren_siem_runbook_v2.pdf) that outlines three supported patterns for private deployments:

1) Customer-forwarder (recommended)
   - Deploy Fluent Bit/Fluentd as a forwarder in Acme's subnet.
   - Forwarder performs TLS termination to the customer's SIEM endpoint (syslog TLS or HEC).
   - Redwood writes token-encrypted payloads to the forwarder over a mutual TLS tunnel (optional) or over an internal, private peering link.
   - Advantages: minimal Redwood egress, customer retains control of retention and PII filtering.

2) Redwood egress via single-NAT egress with mTLS
   - For customers who prefer us to push, Redwood can egress from a dedicated IP pool and present mTLS client certs to the SIEM/HEC endpoint.
   - We support Splunk HEC and RFC-5425 syslog over TLS.
   - Requires customer firewall to allow outbound to our egress IPs and port 443 (HEC) or 6514 (syslog-TLS).

3) Hybrid: push traces to a collector in the VPC and forward logs via syslog
   - Traces: Redwood exports OTLP/JSON spans to a collector inside the VPC over an internal endpoint.
   - Logs: Fluent Bit in the customer's environment does final delivery.

Quick asks for your infra team to confirm:
- Which SIEM endpoint do you prefer (Splunk HEC vs syslog TLS vs Elastic ingest)?
- Do you require mTLS, or is token-based auth sufficient?
- Desired retention and per-hour ingestion rate (we saw a preliminary estimate in your sheet; please confirm).

We'll loop Rishi and Naomi for configuration and network docs.

Best,
Lauren
Head of Customer Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Attachment: lauren_siem_runbook_v2.pdf

-----Internal — Lauren to Rishi, Naomi, Jonas (private)-----
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 May 2028 13:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: SIEM/export requirements for our private deploy

Rishi/Naomi/Jonas — forwarding Acme's asks. Summary: they want Splunk HEC or syslog-TLS; prefer to pin egress to one IP and use mTLS. They also want trace metadata and sampling controls.

Notes for the config/ops side:
- Egress IPs: we can allocate a dedicated NAT pool per-customer in Dedicated mode; confirm number of IPs they require for HA (suggest 2).
- Ports: HEC 443 (HTTPS), syslog-TLS 6514 (TCP). UDP syslog won't be acceptable for them.
- Throughput: their sheet lists 800MB/hour spikey. Assume bursts to 3000 msgs/sec — Fluent Bit batching required.
- Auth: mTLS preferred; we need to coordinate cert provisioning with their security team.

Could you draft minimal Fluent Bit config that: reads from /var/log/redwood/*.log (or our sidecar socket), formats to RFC5424 for syslog, and sends to their syslog-TLS endpoint with client cert and CA pinning. Also include an HEC example for Splunk (token + TLS). Attach sample snippets in reply.

Thanks — happy to be on the call with Acme if needed.
Lauren

-----Technical reply — Rishi Malhotra to group + Acme copy-----
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@acmehealth.com>, Priya Sen <priya.sen@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Security Team <security@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIEM/export requirements for our private deploy

Hi Marco/Priya — copying the config snippets you can hand to your infra folks. We tested these internally against a Splunk HEC sandbox and a syslog-TLS endpoint.

Attachment: fluentbit-config-snippet.conf

Key implementation details:
- Syslog-TLS: use TCP/6514, TLSv1.2+ with mutual auth. We include CA pinning in the agent config and enforce server-name verification.
- Splunk HEC: HTTPS endpoint, token in header (Authorization: Splunk <token>), TLS client cert optional but supported.
- Pin egress: On Redwood Dedicated we can present fixed NAT egress IPs; for Private (VPC) we can coordinate a small egress pool. Please confirm how many IPs Acme expects for failover.
- Traces: Redwood can export OTLP/JSON spans to a customer collector inside the VPC on a non-public endpoint (we'll use VPC peering or private link). The span payload includes trace_id/span_id/service.name/http.status_code. Sampling: default 10% for infra traces; can be increased per-service.

Network firewall rules to allow outbound:
- TCP 443 to <your-HEC-hostname> (if using HEC)
- TCP 6514 to <your-syslog-hostname>
- If using our internal collector endpoint, allow our private-subnet CIDR and mTLS port (we recommend 8443 for OTLP in this pattern).

Security notes:
- We will rotate client certs quarterly by default; short-lived certs on request.
- We can provide an evidence bundle (CSR, cert fingerprints, and test logs) for your audit team during onboarding.

Next steps we suggest:
1) Confirm endpoint choice (HEC vs syslog-TLS) and auth method (token vs mTLS).
2) Confirm desired retention and peak/historical ingestion numbers in the spreadsheet.
3) Schedule a 30-minute connectivity test with your infra.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

-----Final ack from Marco Ruiz (Acme)-----
From: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@acmehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sen <priya.sen@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Security Team <security@acmehealth.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIEM/export requirements for our private deploy

Thanks Rishi/Team — this is exactly what we needed. We'll confirm Splunk HEC + token for now (mTLS as a later step) and update the spreadsheet with throughput numbers.

Can we plan the connectivity test on Thursday at 10:00 PT? Marco and Priya will be on the call. Please send a calendar invite.

Best regards,
Marco
